summary: Names 340B only in answers to comments. The agency declines to set compliance safe harbors for cases where 340B covered entities refuse to share claim data, and notes that one comment concerns the 340B payment adjustment proposed in the 2027 hospital outpatient rule.

Requires 340B covered entities to report Medicare Part D 340B claim data every quarter to a 340B repository run by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, for claims from January 1, 2027. The first required submission is due September 30, 2027.

Sets Medicare hospital outpatient payment for drugs bought under 340B at average sales price minus 28 percent for 2027, where minus 33.4 percent had been proposed. Rural sole community hospitals, children's hospitals and the cancer hospitals paid outside the prospective payment system are exempt. Payments for other services at hospitals subject to the 340B remedy offset are reduced by 2.0 percentage points.
Names 340B only in a summary of comments, where 340B-related income is given as one example of indirect pay that a third-party administrator should disclose to employer health plans.

Would require pharmacy benefit managers' reports to Medicare Part D plans to include a list of the covered drugs that are subject to a 340B agreement with a covered entity, where the manager or an affiliate has a contract or other arrangement with that entity.

Sets up the GLOBE Model, a Medicare Part B drug rebate test, and leaves 340B units out of its rebate count. It keeps the existing 340B claims modifier, TB, to find those units and says 340B itself, including how its price is calculated, is outside the model.

One question in this request for information is about 340B: it asks what standard Medicare Part D pharmacy contract terms say about dispensing to 340B patients, and how plan sponsors decide that a claim is for a 340B patient.
Names 340B only to say that a drug maker must take part in the 340B Program, among other conditions, for its drugs to stay covered by Medicaid. It sets no 340B policy.
Names 340B only in background on hospitals that reclassify from urban to rural, a change that can affect eligibility for programs outside Medicare such as 340B.

Opens a revised 340B Rebate Model Pilot Program. From January 1, 2027, drug makers with an approved plan may give the 340B price as a rebate after the sale, not as a discount up front, on the drugs selected for Medicare price negotiation for 2026 and 2027.

Would require 340B covered entities to report Medicare Part D 340B claim data every quarter to a 340B repository run by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, for claims from January 1, 2027. Reporting was voluntary when this was proposed. Made final at 91 FR 70992.

Would pay hospitals for drugs bought under 340B at average sales price minus 33.4 percent for 2027, with minus 28 percent as an alternative, would exempt rural sole community hospitals, children's hospitals and the cancer hospitals paid outside the prospective payment system, would have hospitals mark 340B drugs with the claim modifier JG, and would raise the 340B remedy offset on other payments from 0.5 percent to 3 percent.
Corrects the June 15, 2026 notice on the rebate pilot's data collection. The total number of responses changes from 793,080 to 793,091 to include the 11 drug maker plan submissions.

Says the rebate pilot's data collection was sent to the Office of Management and Budget for approval, and opens 30 days for comments. It answers the comments on burden made on the earlier 60-day notice.

Names 340B only as a cross-reference. Section 340B(a)(4) of the Public Health Service Act is the list that decides which providers count as essential community providers that health plans on the Exchanges must include in their networks.
Names 340B only in background on hospitals that reclassify from urban to rural, a change that can affect eligibility for programs outside Medicare such as 340B.
Extends the comment period on the February 17, 2026 request for information about a 340B rebate pilot from 30 days to 60 days, so that comments are due April 20, 2026.

Asks for comments on a new data collection for a possible 340B rebate pilot: drug makers' plans, their monthly reports, and claim data from covered entities. It replaces an emergency-cleared collection that the agency ended.

Asks the public whether the agency should use a rebate model for 340B and how to run one, including costs, payment timing, denials, data and duplicate discounts. It says the 2025 pilot was paused after a court order of December 29, 2025.

Names 340B only as a cross-reference. Section 340B(a)(4) of the Public Health Service Act is the list that would decide which providers count as essential community providers that health plans on the Exchanges must include in their networks.

Raises the penalty for each instance of overcharging a 340B covered entity from $7,034 to $7,217, as one row in the yearly inflation adjustment of the Department of Health and Human Services' civil penalties.

Sends a revision of the 340B enrollment and recertification forms to the Office of Management and Budget. New items are collected: grant papers from sexually transmitted disease and tuberculosis grantees, the Title X assistance period, and the Tribal agreement number.

Would set up the GUARD Model, a Medicare Part D drug rebate test, and would leave out drug units covered under 340B. It says the agency cannot yet tell 340B claims apart in Part D data, so it assumed that 10 percent of units were 340B.
Would set up the GLOBE Model, a Medicare Part B drug rebate test, and would leave out units on claims billed with a 340B modifier. Made final at 91 FR 62936.

Keeps the 340B remedy offset on other hospital outpatient payments at 0.5 percent for 2026, where 2 percent had been proposed, and says a survey of what hospitals pay for drugs will open by early 2026.
Names 340B only in a footnote to a table of Medicare Part B trust fund amounts. The footnote says the figures include remedy payments of $10.5 billion to 340B drug providers.
Sets how Medicare removes Part D 340B units from drug inflation rebates starting January 1, 2026, and opens a voluntary 340B repository where covered entities may submit claim data.

Asks for comments, over 60 days, on continuing the 2025 rebate pilot's data collection: drug makers' plans, monthly reports, and the claim data covered entities send to ask for rebates. It says emergency clearance was given on August 26, 2025.

Republishes, as a correction, the August 1, 2025 notice that opened the first 340B rebate pilot. It moves the comment deadline to September 8, 2025 and fills in the docket number. A court set that pilot aside on February 10, 2026.

Proposes revising the 340B enrollment and recertification forms, and takes comments until October 6, 2025. New items would be collected: grant papers from sexually transmitted disease and tuberculosis grantees, the Title X assistance period, and the Tribal agreement number.
Names 340B only in background on hospitals that reclassify from urban to rural, a change that can affect eligibility for programs outside Medicare such as 340B.

Opens the first 340B rebate pilot. Drug makers with Medicare negotiation agreements for 2026 could apply to pay rebates, not discounts up front, on selected drugs from January 1, 2026. A court set this notice aside on February 10, 2026.
Would raise the 340B remedy offset on other hospital outpatient payments from 0.5 percent to 2 percent for 2026, and announces a survey of what hospitals pay for drugs.
Would remove Part D 340B units from Medicare drug inflation rebates starting January 1, 2026, by matching claims, and would set up a voluntary 340B repository for covered entities' claim data.

Executive Order 14273. Section 7 tells the Secretary of Health and Human Services to make future health center grants depend on offering insulin and injectable epinephrine to certain low-income patients at or below the price the health center paid under 340B, plus a minimal administration fee.
Names 340B only in background on hospitals that reclassify from urban to rural, a change that can affect eligibility for programs outside Medicare such as 340B.

Names 340B only in the Medicare drug price negotiation payment process, where a drug maker may show that a 340B discount applies, and in comments on overlap with the 340B ceiling price, which the agency calls out of scope.
Sends a data collection to the Office of Management and Budget for the papers a covered entity or drug maker files to start a 340B Administrative Dispute Resolution claim, with 30 days for comments.
